P1.evidence: Setter acknowledged but nothing read back: 'i know you spoke with kyla... she gave me like a head start so i feel like i understand a little bit'. Frame was three-part — 'go a bit deeper, get some context, and then build out what it is that you want, and if we can help, then we can talk about it. Some people we can't, and that's fine too' — with 'what's in the way' missing. Agreement asked ('alrighty?') and given ('Cool'), then the open question.

P2.evidence: The injury probe was the best in the batch — 'Talk to me about the mobility. I know you said lower back. I want to make sure I have context of everything' — which produced the 2010 disc bulge, the duration, the triggers and the chiropractic care. Results from current approach were interrogated properly, including a before/after photo review and the observation that he had lost muscle as well as fat. But age, height, work, general health conditions, diet, sleep and energy were never asked; weight, body fat, age (45) and 'I have always been a IT consultant' were all volunteered.

P3.evidence: The 'what shifted' bridge ran well — 'What I'm curious about the most is what shifted for you to want to, like, re-streamline' — producing the planning-versus-execution admission. The North Star was summarised back ('you want abs, build muscle, feel confident in terms of your body's capability') and the mechanism was reflected back sharply ('the mobility is the linchpin'). But the deep why never got touched: the prospect said at 00:01:15 'I have two boys, 19 and 14... It's a matter of time. I got to keep up. I'm 45 now' and the rep never returned to it once in fifty minutes.

P4.evidence: Strong root-cause work on the real blocker: 'you have a level of uncertainty which needs to be overcome' ('Yes, yes. That's what it is') and 'is that another reason why you're kind of like, hey, I kind of want to coach with it? Because you don't want to test it yourself and screw it' ('Yes, 100%. 100%'). Prior attempts (gym, HIIT) were surfaced but never worked through, and the 'why can't you stick to it on your own' question never ran.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame. The prospect handed over the exact raw material — five months lost with nothing to show, a back that has been degrading since 2010, two teenage sons and 'I got to keep up' — and none of it was converted into a cost of inaction. On a call that ends on a $2,000 competitor comparison, this is the phase that would have decided it.

P6.evidence: A soft commitment statement was made rather than a question before presenting — 'It sounds like you've come to the point where you know you need to commit to change' ('Yeah') — and the actual belief question only ran after the price landed: 'The most important part of everything, do you feel like we can actually help you get where you want to go?' ('I believe so'). The 'if you had everything you needed, any reason you wouldn't go all in' question never ran, so nothing was locked down before the number.

P11.evidence: Close attempted — price, guarantee, and a good logistical pre-close ('we would get you all onboarded before you go. You have your call with Trevor before you go') — but payment was never asked for, not once. The call ended on 'How long do you feel like you need to wrap your head around things?' with no follow-up date booked. Once payment was deferred the remaining onboarding steps were unreachable.

objection_plays.detail: 'That's the most expensive I've ever heard' and 'it's quite steep' landed hard. The rep did two useful things — clarified the objection ('do you mean like, you don't think it's worth it, or you just weren't expecting it?') and ran the belief question. Beyond that the play did not run: no 'finances aside, nothing else keeping you from 100%' isolation, no SHOULD-I versus HOW frame, no financial picture, and critically the opposite of the scripted 'most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up' — when asked directly he said 'It's six months, one shot.'

'Let me work that out... digest' is a think-about-it in substance. The rep time-boxed it ('How long do you feel like you need to wrap your head around things?') and removed the travel obstacle by offering to onboard before departure, but ran none of the OA moves — no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no 'are you sure, nothing else keeping you from being 100% in'. No follow-up call was booked at the end.

The decisive objection was a like-for-like competitor at $2,000 for a year with one-on-one coaching, nutrition and weekly check-ins — the known script gap in its clearest form yet (five times cheaper, not a $29/mo app). The rep asked the single best available question, 'why didn't you do the one that was 2K for a year?', and then did not use the answer: he had already established the prospect will not train his lower body unsupervised, and never converted that into why a generic or cheaper provider cannot solve the back. He fell back on 'I can't decide that for you.'

Clinical fit: a 2010 disc bulge under active chiropractic care, with the prospect explicitly frightened of loading. There is no scripted path, and the rep improvised by underwriting it himself — disclosing his own scoliosis as common ground, normalising lumbar involvement in swings as 'just a tweak you have to make', and telling him blood work was unnecessary. He then used the back to disqualify the cheaper group programme, which is commercially deft and clinically unsupported in both directions.

notes: The strongest diagnostic call in the batch — genuine root-cause work that identified fear of loading the back as the real blocker, and an excellent question aimed at the competitor quote. It then fell over in the same two places every call in this batch does: no consequence frame, and no ask for the money. Two specific corrections: the deep why was handed to him at minute one (two sons, 'I got to keep up') and never used, and telling a price-sensitive prospect that payment is one-shot closed off the payment plan that other calls treat as available.
